newsitem.title: GEORGIA: EBRD says it will triple investment in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: EBRD says it will triple investment in Georgia.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will triple its investment projects in Georgia to $150 million, Bank president Jacques de Larosiere said on Thursday.
"The EBRD's visit in Georgia was extremely useful and convinced me about the necessity for further investment projects in different economic spheres of the republic," he told reporters.
He said the EBRD, which has invested about $50 million in Georgia since 1994, will concentrate on future projects in private enterprises, transport, energy and construction.
He said he expected overall financing to triple to $150 million in 1997-98.
Among these future projects are the construction of a grain terminal in the port of Poti and credit support for Georgian banks, de Larosiere said.
De Larosiere said he was confident that a $12-$16 million investment this year would create a Caucasus investment fund to help small and medium-sized businesses.
The EBRD was also considering financing an oil pipeline through Georgia, he said.

During de Larosiere's visit the EBRD opened a credit line of $1 million to Tbiluniversalbank and $5 million to the Georgian-American Absolyutbank, the first commercial bank in the former Soviet Union.
Absolyutbank secured the credit without state guarantees.

The principal EBRD Georgia projects to date have been the rehabilitation of the energy sector, the reconstruction of the Tbilisi airport, setting up a credit line for small and medium business through commercial banks, and the opening of a commercial bank.
